text:
Add GBrain memory to this existing agent. Read and follow:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md
Keep my current identity and instructions, start keyless, and show me the
search-mode choice. Verify a remember/recall round trip with real GBrain calls.

Install gbrain release v0.60.757.0 (`github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0`) wherever the docs say #stable.
reply_text:
GBrain is installed and connected to this Hermes agent. Your identity text is unchanged, the brain has no API keys, and remember/recall works through both the CLI and the MCP server Hermes uses. One check didn't finish: a fresh `hermes -z` session timed out, even on a trivial prompt.

What I set up:
- **Version:** gbrain 0.60.757.0, at /harness-state/.local/bin/gbrain. Hermes's scanner blocks `bun install -g github:…`, so I used the docs' release-binary route. The binary comes straight from the v0.60.757.0 tag, which is what you pinned.
- **Brain:** a local PGLite database at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite, created with `--no-embedding`, so it has no keys and uses keyword search only. The pending setup migrations have been applied.
- **Hermes wiring:** `gbrain setup hermes` registered gbrain as an MCP server in config.yaml. It also added the docs' per-turn "check GBrain first" hook (`pre_llm_call`).
  - Setup ended with a `turn_hook_not_loaded` error.
  - Hermes's own check, `hermes hooks doctor`, says the hook is healthy and approved, and `gbrain doctor` reports it as "wired". So I'm treating that error as a false alarm.
- **Identity:** your original SOUL.md line is still first and word-for-word the same. gbrain added a marked block below it; `gbrain setup hermes --remove` takes it out.

Round trip, with real calls:
- **CLI:** `remember` saved fact #1 ("gbrain install check: …"), and `recall --query "gbrain install check"` returned it with provenance `install-check`.
- **MCP:** `hermes mcp test gbrain` connected and found 8 tools, including remember, recall and entity. Over that same server command I saved fact #2 (token hx-7731), and `recall` returned facts #2 and #1.

Open item: `hermes -z` timed out after 120–280 s even on "Reply with just: ok", so I couldn't confirm a new session calls the tools on its own. That looks like a problem with running Hermes nested inside this headless session, not with gbrain. In a new interactive session, ask it to "recall gbrain install check" to confirm. The tools only load when a session starts, which is also why this one can't call them.

Search mode: it's set to conservative. With no chat key and no reranker key, that's the mode gbrain picks. You can change it any time with `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>`:

    Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:

                      Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                      ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
      conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
      balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
      tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo

      Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
      Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.

    1) conservative (in effect): 4K token budget, 10 chunks, no reranker.
    2) balanced: 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked. Needs a Voyage key.
    3) tokenmax: no budget, 50 chunks, reranked. The widest retrieval.

Since this brain has no keys, balanced and tokenmax won't rerank until you add a Voyage key. Running `gbrain search modes` shows the active mode.

Other defaults now in effect (you can change these whenever):
- **Saving facts:** off, so it only saves what you ask it to remember. gbrain recommends `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`.
- **Upkeep:** free upkeep is on. `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false` turns it off.
- **Conversation archive:** on, stored locally. `gbrain transcripts archive off` turns it off.
- **Skills:** the bundled skills weren't scaffolded.

Hosted GBrain at gbrain.io is an always-on alternative if you'd rather not run the brain locally.

The two test facts are #1 and #2. Remove them with `gbrain forget` when you're done.
